category: AI Agents, Tool Calling & Model Context Protocol (MCP)

diagram_caption: ReAct cycle: interleaved Thought, Action, and Observation states.

content.tldr: An AI agent couples an LLM core with memory, planning, and external tool execution, using the ReAct (Reason + Act) loop to interleave natural language thought with environment actions.
content.simple_explanation: Unlike a passive conversational model that emits a single prompt response, an AI agent operates autonomously in an environment. The ReAct paradigm structures the execution trace into alternating phases: Thought (the model analyzes the goal and decomposes the next sub-step), Action (the model outputs a structured tool invocation like a database query or web search), and Observation (the runtime feeds the tool execution output back into context).
content.real_world_example: A software debugging agent: Thought: 'I should inspect the failing test trace.' Action: 'run_command(pytest tests/test_auth.py)'. Observation: 'ImportError: no module named jwt'. Thought: 'JWT dependency is missing; I need to inspect pyproject.toml.'
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Without strict termination conditions and loop detection, agents can enter infinite loops repeating failing tool calls. Always enforce maximum iteration limits and catch tool execution exceptions gracefully.
